title: In-house Programmes in MOE Kindergartens for Special Needs Children
what_it_is: In-house Programmes in MOE Kindergartens for Special Needs Children

sections.label: MKs use Early Intervention provisions
sections.summary: MKs tap on sector-wide Early Intervention provisions like DS-LS and DS-Plus to support these children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: MKs tap on sector-wide Early Intervention (EI) provisions, such as the Development Support - Learning Support (DS-LS) and Development Support Plus (DS-Plus) programmes, to support these children.

sections.label: Progress to mainstream or SPED
sections.summary: Most children with developmental needs progress to mainstream Primary schools, while MOE Educational Psychologists may recommend SPED for a small proportion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Education (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: While the majority of children with developmental needs will progress to mainstream Primary schools, MOE Educational Psychologists will also make recommendations to Special Education (SPED) for the small proportion of children better supported in a SPED school.

sections.label: MK Educators baseline training
sections.summary: MK Educators receive baseline training from MOE Educational Psychologists within their first two years of service on developmental needs and support strategies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: MKs are part of the wider ecosystem of preschools for children, especially those with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And in our MKs, the MK Educators are offered baseline training by MOE Educational Psychologists within the first two years of service to gain awareness of developmental needs and strategies to support these diverse learners in the classroom.

sections.label: Support for children with special needs
sections.summary: The aim is the best support for children with special needs in MKs or early intervention centres, working with centres so programmes are complementary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We want the best support for children with special needs, whether they are in MKs or in the EIPIC centres or the early intervention centres that Member Denise Phua mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And we will work together with the early intervention centres to make sure the programmes and support given to the special needs children will be complementary.

sections.label: MK special needs support and spectrum
sections.summary: The waitlist for special needs children wanting MKs is unknown, but all MKs have trained teachers and professional support, with care supplemented for moderate and severe conditions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Offhand I do not know the waitlist for special needs children who want to go to the MKs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: But, as I mentioned earlier on, all MKs have specially trained teachers and are supported by a group of professionals to help students with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And also, we know that among special needs students, there is actually a very wide spectrum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Those that are of very mild conditions; most of them are able to get the support that they need from the MKs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And those who are deemed to have moderate and more severe conditions, their care and support will then be supplemented by the other centres that the students will go to once or twice a week.
